bullets.title: Finally started playing with Procreate
bullets.note: This is [my first attempt](https://www.instagram.com/p/CsAGywLNaZV/) at a quick, original piece. My old friend Bacchus was kind enough to pose. I still have a LOT to learn, and I’m awkward with the tools, but it makes me really happy to start sketching again. Anyone have any favorite video tutorials for [Procreate](https://procreate.com/) out there? If so, please do let me know in the comments [here](https://www.instagram.com/p/CsAGywLNaZV/).

bullets.title: Jura ENA 4
bullets.note:
(Cost: $999). This was gifted to me by my friend Brad L. He is a die-hard coffee nerd and swore it was the best cup of coffee you could have without a professional barista. Just feed it whole beans, and it handles the rest. This attractive machine also imbues the coffee with a creamy texture that is hard to describe.  
​  
​[**AeroPress** **Original**](https://aeropress.com/products/aeropress-coffee-maker) (Cost: <$40). This is an incredible, and affordable, little gem. As I wrote in [_The 4-Hour Chef_](https://www.amazon.com/4-Hour-Chef-Cooking-Learning-Anything/dp/1328519163/): “This is now, bar none, my favorite brewing method. Remember the Aerobie, the amazing UFO-like disc that you could throw farther than a football field, 20 times farther than a standard Frisbee? Alan Adler, a mechanical engineer and Stanford University lecturer, created it. After conquering the 1980s toy market, he began to obsess over coffee. The result was the AeroPress, which debuted in 2006. Quickly adopted by the specialty coffee community, it offers a simple way to prepare a small amount of excellent coffee, and it’s great for travel. Armed with an AeroPress and a tiny manual hand grinder like the [Hario MSS-1B Mini Mill](https://www.amazon.com/Hario-Mini-Mill-Coffee-Grinder/dp/B001804CLY?th=1) \[or the more recently recommended [Comandante](https://www.comandantegrinder.com/)\], you can even make world-class coffee on an airplane meal tray! No mess and no fuss.” If you want to use a beefier and automated burr grinder at home, I now use the [Baratza Encore](https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B084HNY3BG/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&th=1).

bullets.title: “If you can’t read and write, you can’t think. Your thoughts are dispersed if you don’t know how to read and write. You’ve got to be able to look at your thoughts on paper and discover what a fool you were.” — Ray Bradbury (Click here to share on Twitter.) * * * You can complement this edition of 5-Bullet Friday with my coffee-making appearance on Late Night with Jimmy Fallon_, my short video on journaling and taking notes, and some of my comic book posters that I’ve kept to this day. And, as always, please give me feedback on Twitter. Which bullet above is your favorite? What do you want more or less of? Other suggestions? Please let me know. Just send a tweet to @tferriss and put #5BulletFriday at the end so I can find it. Have a wonderful weekend, all. Much love to you and yours, Tim
